---
applyTo: "packages/islands/**"
---

Expose only `/build` and `/react` as public package entry points. Application code registers XML paths with `pluginIslands({ exposes })` and renders `<Island name="card" props={data} />`. Keep loading, readiness, container selectors, native commit options and the useIsland hook internal. The component generates a stable container ID with ReactLynx useId; applications control disposal by unmounting it.

Import useId from @lynx-js/react/hooks, where the installed package exposes its types and Rspeedy maps the implementation to each thread. The root @lynx-js/react entry does not currently export this hook.

`pluginIslands` accepts an exposes map with XML path strings as the default form; parse Lynx XML inside the plugin. Infrastructure integrations may supply a source and custom parser object. Append sections to the host entry selected by entry (default main), preserving existing host sections and detecting duplicates. The main-thread wrapper supplies the lexical __lynxIsland marker. Each internal module create() call returns fresh render, update, dispose, and optional setBackgroundReady state.

Keep inline and remote delivery on the same exposes map, shared XML parser, section naming, module factory and Island component. Default to inline sections in the host entry; output.mode remote emits all exposes as a separate bundle resource. Resource-only producers must build with Rsbuild and the Islands plugin without ReactLynx, a React plugin or an application entry. The Island component's optional entry URL selects a remote resource; hosted rendering always shares the existing Page and runtime. Do not add a second public runtime API or a standalone-page mode.

Keep module loading independent from instance creation. Load and evaluate the exposed main section synchronously, adopt its page-scoped stylesheet, then initialize the background section. Creating an instance owns native nodes, listeners and disposal. One loaded module supports concurrent instances in different containers.

Keep background readiness independent from main rendering. Use **Card** for inline sections and the resolved fetchBundle URL for remote scripts and styles. Cache background initialization by bundle identity and expose, clear failed entries for retry, and distinguish scripts with different contents in the native tt module registry. ResponseHandler.then accepts a single callback and returns void; wrap it explicitly instead of chaining or awaiting the handler. Subscribe before dispatching and release readiness listeners after success, failure or page destruction. Native handles and readiness promises stay on their owning threads.

Use the shared `@lynx-js/lynx-xml/parser` result for exposed source parsing. Keep XML grammar and offset diagnostics in that package; convert its raw CSS in the Islands build layer with the existing CSS serializer. Reject unsupported at-rules and unresolved stylesheet imports before serialization, preserve optional empty sections, and avoid coupling this native build path to `web-core/encode`.

Render inline modules synchronously from the main-thread container ref using initial serializable props. Remote loads are asynchronous and their initial render must flush independently of the host's first-screen commit. Retain the module or pending load and instance inside MainThreadRef for hydration reuse; coalesce pending props, include entry and expose in identity, and invalidate stale rendering on resource switches, unmount or page destruction. Queue background preparation through the existing runOnBackground hydration mechanism. Test real compiled worklet hydration without changing the ReactLynx runtime.

When testing compiled worklet hydration directly with `@lynx-js/react/worklet-runtime/bindings`, initialize the global compile-time flags required by the installed ReactLynx runtime, including `__PROFILE__`, before invoking `runWorklet`.

Callback refs can detach and reattach during hydration. Preserve an inline instance when the same native container receives the new ref: resolve the container selector against the existing page and compare its native unique ID, then defer final detached cleanup until the current synchronous ref handoff has finished. Read identity without writing an EOM owner attribute, because an attribute write would schedule an extra flush. A different native container must dispose the previous renderer immediately. Keep a compiled-worklet regression test that exercises detach, context hydration, reattach, and delayed background activation.

Keep the internal module create() argument-free. Its renderer accepts a per-render flush option defaulting to true. Pass false only during the synchronous main-thread initial render whose native commit belongs to the host. Later renders, updates, asynchronous results and disposal own their commits. Do not expose these details to application code or add worklet scheduling integration. Compare serialized props across hydration, skip identical updates and invalidate failed snapshots for retry.

Observe main-thread page destruction through lynx.getNative(), not getEngine(). Do not install a native __DestroyLifetime listener on the background thread, because that can suppress the host's normal background destruction lifecycle.

Store the React adapter's serialized props snapshot directly as a scalar. Reserve null for an invalidated snapshot, distinct from JSON.stringify returning undefined. On update failure, invalidate only when the instance and serialized value still match; this is a conservative deduplication cache, not committed UI state. Cover retrying identical props after failure and preserving a newer different snapshot.

Exposed XML changes during development must change the host compilation hash and trigger a full page reload, because ordinary JavaScript HMR cannot replace the already loaded custom sections. Prepend a self-declined fingerprint module to the selected host entry, preserving its layer and application exports. Keep the marker out of builds and dev sessions with both HMR and live reload disabled. Initialize virtual files through the VirtualModulesPlugin constructor, write only when their content changes, and include the marker in modifiedFiles for the current rebuild so batched changes cannot leave it cached. Cover actual Rspack watch compilations for main script, background script and style changes, and verify the HMR abort with a self-accepted application entry.
